eligibility_text: Appel à projets 2024-2025 « vers la stratégie nationale pour l’alimentation, la nutrition et le climat (SNANC) ». Trois volets : Volet 1 « émergence de nouveaux Projets Alimentaires Territoriaux » - « La sélection des nouveaux PAT sera exigeante notamment sur la prise en compte de tous les objectifs fixés par la loi » ; Volet 2 « développement d’actions innovantes pour l’alimentation » - « Le caractère particulièrement innovant à l’échelle nationale et le potentiel d’essaimage » ; Volet 3 « essaimage à grande échelle de démarches exemplaires » - « Les projets devront s’appuyer sur des initiatives ayant fait la preuve de leur efficacité ». Pour les volets 2 et 3, seuls les projets structurants d’envergure nationale ou interrégionale sont éligibles. Enveloppe globale pouvant atteindre 2,8 millions d’euros. Ouverture le 13 novembre 2024, clôture le 8 janvier 2025.

eligibility_text: Êtes-vous concerné ? Les structures éligibles dans le cadre de cet appel à projets sont les organismes de conseil . Elles peuvent être publiques, associatives et/ou privées (ex : chambres d’agriculture, coopérative agricole, association de développement agricole, mandataires du label bas carbone, instituts techniques agricoles, industries agro-alimentaires, interprofession, organismes et associations de gestion et de comptabilité, structure juridique reconnue GIEE, CIVAM…). Dans tous les cas, le bénéficiaire final de l’aide (c’est-à-dire le bénéficiaire du conseil / diagnostic) doit être une PME active dans la production agricole primaire, comprenant : les agriculteurs, personnes physiques ou morales (GAEC, EARL, SARL, etc.) les lycées agricoles et les exploitations agricoles des établissements d’enseignement agricole les groupements d’agriculteurs ayant une production agricole primaire, de type GIE ou CUMA (composées à 100 % d’agriculteurs)

eligibility_text: Vous souhaitez contribuer au déploiement des politiques de l'ADEME ? Les aides aux relais pourront vous permettre de recruter un poste de chargé de mission ! Voici des exemples de profils de postes : animateur filière Bois-énergie, chargé de mission EnR, animateur solaire thermique, chargé de mission qualité de l'air, conseiller en mobilité, animateur Biodéchets, animateur filière Méthanisation, animateur alimentation durable, relai Agri-énergie, chargé de mission EIT, etc. Les aides aux actions ponctuelles pourront financer vos actions ponctuelles d'animation, de communication et/ou de formation. description:
Vous disposez d’une **étude de faisabilité pour votre projet d'installation de production de chaleur biomasse/bois** et vous souhaitez investir pour le mettre en œuvre ? Cette aide est destinée à subventionner votre installation.

Projets liés au dispositif d'aide :
Chauffage au bois

Montant de l'aide ou cout: Selon projet

Contact public pour les questions sur le dispositif: https://fondschaleur.ademe.fr/contact/

Etapes pour activer le dispositif :
Consultez la documentation de l’ADEME pour vérifier l’éligibilité de votre projet ou contactez un conseiller.
Liens liés à l'étape : [Conditions éligibilité et financement](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/sites/default/files/Installation%20biomasse%20%C3%A9nergie%20-%20Conditions%20d%27%C3%A9ligibilit%C3%A9%20et%20de%20financement%202026.pdf)
Créez un compte ADEME pour pouvoir déposer votre dossier.
Liens liés à l'étape : [Créer mon compte ADEME](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/user/register)
Déposez votre dossier avant le 15 mai 2025 à 15h00 : informations administratives, description du projet, détails techniques et financiers, etc. À ce stade, votre projet ne doit pas avoir commencé !
Liens liés à l'étape : [Déposer mon dossier](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/entreprises/aides-financieres/2024/realisation-dinstallations-production-chaleur-biomasse-bois?cible=79)
L'ADEME étudie votre demande en fonction de l’étude du projet, de l’approvisionnement biomasse, de la quantité de chaleur produite et de ses performances énergétiques et environnementales.
Si votre demande est acceptée, recevez un contrat de financement précisant le montant d’aide maximum, les conditions et les modalités de versement.
Réalisez vos investissements.

description:
Vous pensez disposer de chaleur perdue sans savoir comment la valoriser ? Vous souhaitez mettre en place une installation de récupération de chaleur fatale ?\
L’ADEME peut financer une **étude de faisabilité**, étape indispensable avant tout investissement. Elle permet de :\
– **identifier les solutions techniques adaptées à votre site**,\
– **analyser les options de montage financier, administratif et juridique**.

Cet accompagnement vous aide à évaluer la pertinence de votre projet et à prendre des décisions éclairées pour optimiser vos ressources énergétiques.

Projets liés au dispositif d'aide :
Chaleur de récupération

Montant de l'aide ou cout: Jusqu'à 70% du coût de l'étude, dans un maximum de 100 000 €

Contact public pour les questions sur le dispositif: https://fondschaleur.ademe.fr/contact/

Consultez la documentation de l’ADEME pour vérifier l’éligibilité de votre projet ou contactez un conseiller.

Créez un compte ADEME pour pouvoir déposer votre dossier.
Liens liés à l'étape : [Créer mon compte ADEME](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/user/register)
Déposez votre dossier : informations administratives, description du projet, détails techniques et financiers, etc. À ce stade, votre projet ne doit pas avoir commencé !
Liens liés à l'étape : [Déposer mon dossier](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/entreprises/aides-financieres/2025/etudes-faisabilite-linstallation-recuperation-chaleur-fatale)

description:
Vous souhaitez installer une toiture ou ombrière solaire photovoltaïque en autoconsommation individuelle ?\
Lorsque la consommation électrique de vos bâtiments et équipements se fait principalement de jour, il peut être intéressant d’étudier la faisabilité de couvrir une partie de cette consommation grâce à l’électricité solaire.

L’ADEME peut accompagner le financement d’études de faisabilité externes pour :

- **évaluer et analyser le potentiel du projet**,

- **identifier ses forces, faiblesses, opportunités et menaces**,

- estimer les **ressources nécessaires à sa réalisation**.

Cette démarche vous aide à sécuriser votre investissement et à mieux préparer la mise en œuvre.

Projets liés au dispositif d'aide :
Panneaux solaires

Montant de l'aide ou cout: Jusqu'à 80% du coût de l'étude, dans un maximum de 100 000 € HT

Contact public pour les questions sur le dispositif: https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/form/contact?id_dsp=DSP000728

Choisissez le bureau d'étude énergétique qui va vous accompagner pour mener cette étude de faisabilité et faites réaliser un devis.
Créez un compte ADEME pour pouvoir déposer votre dossier.
Liens liés à l'étape : [Créer mon compte ADEME](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/user/register)
Déposez votre dossier : informations administratives, description du projet, détails techniques et financiers, etc. À ce stade, votre projet ne doit pas avoir commencé !
Liens liés à l'étape : [Déposer mon dossier](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/entreprises/aides-financieres/2025/etudes-faisabilite-lautoconsommation-electrique-photovoltaique)

description:
L’ADEME vous aide à financer un audit énergétique sur le périmètre de votre choix : site de production, atelier ou process.

L’audit énergétique vous permet :

-  **de réaliser un état des lieux complet de vos consommations**, pour mieux comprendre où et comment l’énergie est utilisée ;
-  **d’identifier les postes les plus énergivores**, en croisant les données techniques et économiques ;
- **de définir et hiérarchiser les actions les plus efficaces**, selon leur rentabilité, leur temps de retour sur investissement et leur facilité de mise en œuvre.

Projets liés au dispositif d'aide :
Audit énergétique
Management de l’énergie

Montant de l'aide ou cout: Jusqu'à 80% du coût de l'étude, dans un maximum de 100 000 €

Contact public pour les questions sur le dispositif: https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/form/contact?id_dsp=DSP000852

Etapes pour activer le dispositif :
Consultez la documentation de l’ADEME pour vérifier l’éligibilité de votre projet ou contactez un conseiller.
Liens liés à l'étape : [Conditions éligibilité et financement](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/sites/default/files/PACTE%20Entreprises%20-%20Audit%20%C3%A9nerg%C3%A9tique%20-%20Conditions%20d%27%C3%A9ligibilit%C3%A9%20et%20de%20financement%20-%202026.pdf)
Choisissez un auditeur énergétique "Reconnu Garant de l'Environnement" (RGE), et obtenez un devis.
Liens liés à l'étape : [Annuaire des professionnels RGE](https://france-renov.gouv.fr/annuaires-professionnels/artisan-rge-architecte)
Créez un compte ADEME pour pouvoir déposer votre dossier.
Liens liés à l'étape : [Créer mon compte ADEME](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/user/register)
Déposez votre dossier : informations administratives, description du projet, détails techniques et financiers, etc. À ce stade, votre projet ne doit pas avoir commencé !
Liens liés à l'étape : [Déposer mon dossier](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/entreprises/aides-financieres/catalogue/2026/pacte-entreprises-audit-energetique-volontaire-en-industrie)
L'ADEME étudie votre demande d'aide. Si votre demande est acceptée, recevez un contrat de financement précisant le montant d’aide maximum, les conditions et les modalités de versement.
Réalisez votre audit énergétique. Vous disposerez d'un état des lieux complet de vos consommations, des pistes d'amélioration sous forme de plan d'action ainsi que les gains économiques associés et leurs temps de retour sur investissement.

description:

- **évaluer les actions correctives et financer les travaux de remise en service**.

Cette aide vous permet de restaurer rapidement les performances de votre installation, de réduire son impact environnemental et de retrouver une production d’eau chaude économique et durable.

Chauffe-eau solaire

-  **identifier les techniques adaptées aux caractéristiques de votre site**,
- **connaître les solutions pour le montage financier, administratif et juridique** de votre projet.

Elle vous aide ainsi à sécuriser votre investissement et à choisir la solution la plus pertinente.

Projets liés au dispositif d'aide :
Pompe à chaleur
Géothermie

Montant de l'aide ou cout: Jusqu'à 70% du coût de l'étude, dans un maximum de 100 000 €

Le montant, le coût ou la durée de l'aide peuvent varier en fonction de la taille de l'entreprise

Contact public pour les questions sur le dispositif: https://fondschaleur.ademe.fr/contact/

Etapes pour activer le dispositif :
Consultez la documentation de l’ADEME pour vérifier l’éligibilité de votre projet ou contactez un conseiller.
Liens liés à l'étape : [Conditions éligibilité et financement](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/sites/default/files/%C3%89tudes%20en%20faveur%20de%20la%20transition%20%C3%A9cologique%20-%20Conditions%20d%27%C3%A9ligibilit%C3%A9%20et%20de%20financement%20-%202026.pdf)
Choisissez un auditeur énergétique "Reconnu Garant de l'Environnement" (RGE) ou équivalent, et obtenez un devis.
Liens liés à l'étape : [Annuaire des professionnels RGE](https://france-renov.gouv.fr/annuaires-professionnels/artisan-rge-architecte)
Créez un compte ADEME pour pouvoir déposer votre dossier.
Liens liés à l'étape : [Créer mon compte ADEME](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/user/register)
Déposez votre dossier : informations administratives, description du projet, détails techniques et financiers, etc. À ce stade, votre projet ne doit pas avoir commencé !
Liens liés à l'étape : [Déposer mon dossier](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/entreprises/aides-financieres/catalogue/2026/etude-daide-la-decision-pour-les-projets-de-geothermie-de-surface-daerothermie-ou-de-thalassothermie)
L'ADEME étudie votre demande d'aide. Si votre demande est acceptée, recevez un contrat de financement précisant le montant d’aide maximum, les conditions et les modalités de versement.
Réalisez votre étude pour vérifier la faisabilité technique et économique de votre projet d'implantation d’une installation de géothermie de surface et aérothermie.


Lien externe de présentation de l'aide https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/entreprises/aides-financieres/catalogue/2026/etude-daide-la-decision-pour-les-projets-de-geothermie-de-surface-daerothermie-ou-de-thalassothermie

description:
Vous souhaitez concevoir un produit ou service à faible impact environnemental ? L’ADEME peut financer une **étude d’éco-conception** pour structurer une démarche d’amélioration sur l’ensemble du cycle de vie.

Cette étude permet de :\
– **identifier les leviers de réduction des impacts** à chaque étape (matières premières, fabrication, usage, fin de vie),\
– **intégrer les enjeux environnementaux dès la conception**, en tenant compte des compromis techniques, économiques et écologiques.

Elle vous aide à faire des choix durables, différenciants et adaptés à votre activité.

Projets liés au dispositif d'aide :
Numérique responsable
Écoconception d’un produit ou service
Allongement de la durée de vie

Montant de l'aide ou cout: Jusqu'à 80% du coût de l'étude, dans un maximum de 100 000 €

Contact public pour les questions sur le dispositif: https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/form/contact?id_dsp=DSP000901

Consultez la documentation de l’ADEME pour vérifier l’éligibilité de votre projet ou contactez un conseiller.
Liens liés à l'étape : [Conditions éligibilité et financement](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/sites/default/files/%C3%89tudes%20%C3%89coconception%20-%20Conditions%20d%27%C3%A9ligibilit%C3%A9%20et%20de%20financement%20-%202026.pdf)
Choisissez le prestataire qui va vous accompagner pour mener cette étude et obtenez un devis.
Créez un compte ADEME pour pouvoir déposer votre dossier.
Liens liés à l'étape : [Créer mon compte ADEME](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/user/register)
Déposez votre dossier : informations administratives, description du projet, détails techniques et financiers, etc. À ce stade, votre projet ne doit pas avoir commencé !
Liens liés à l'étape : [Déposer mon dossier](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/entreprises/aides-financieres/2025/etudes-decoconception-produits-services)

description:
Vous cherchez à mieux gérer vos **biodéchets** et à en faire une ressource ? La CCI Hauts-de-France vous accompagne pour identifier les solutions de réduction et de valorisation adaptées à votre activité. Cet accompagnement vous aide à structurer une démarche concrète et efficace.

- Analysez la **nature, le volume et la fréquence** de vos biodéchets, ainsi que leur localisation.

- Repérez les solutions de **valorisation proches de chez vous** : compostage, méthanisation, etc.

- Référencez vos flux sur une **plateforme géolocalisée** dédiée pour faciliter les synergies locales.

- Bénéficiez d’un **outil d’aide à la décision** pour choisir les solutions techniques, repérer les dispositifs de financement mobilisables, et entrer en contact avec les bons interlocuteurs.

Projets liés au dispositif d'aide :
Gestion des biodéchets
Zéro perte en production

Durée de l'aide: De 1 à 5 jours selon la taille et le secteur d'activité de l'entreprise

Le programme PACTE Industrie accompagne les industriels dans leur transition énergétique grâce à des études et un coaching personnalisés.

Il vous aide notamment à :

- réaliser des **études d’opportunité** sur le mix énergétique,

- élaborer une **stratégie de décarbonation** ambitieuse,

- construire un **plan de financement** adapté à vos projets.

Management de l’énergie

- Passez à la **phase d’industrialisation** : production, assemblage, réparation, et reconditionnement des véhicules tout en affinant le design.

- Identifiez les **sources de financement** régionales, nationales ou de l’ADEME pour soutenir les différentes phases de votre projet.

- Bénéficiez des nombreuses **expertises du réseau** : mécanique, design, électronique, urbanisme, ecoconception, modèles économiques, communication, marketing, etc.

description:
Vous disposez d’une **étude de faisabilité pour votre projet d'installation de production de chaleur biomasse/bois** et vous souhaitez investir pour le mettre en œuvre ? Cette aide est destinée à subventionner votre installation.

Projets liés au dispositif d'aide :
Chauffage au bois

Montant de l'aide ou cout: Selon projet

Contact public pour les questions sur le dispositif: https://fondschaleur.ademe.fr/contact/

Etapes pour activer le dispositif :
Consultez la documentation de l’ADEME pour vérifier l’éligibilité de votre projet ou contactez un conseiller.
Liens liés à l'étape : [Conditions éligibilité et financement](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/sites/default/files/Installation%20biomasse%20%C3%A9nergie%20-%20Conditions%20d%27%C3%A9ligibilit%C3%A9%20et%20de%20financement%202026.pdf)
Créez un compte ADEME pour pouvoir déposer votre dossier.
Liens liés à l'étape : [Créer mon compte ADEME](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/user/register)
Déposez votre dossier avant le 15 mai 2025 à 15h00 : informations administratives, description du projet, détails techniques et financiers, etc. À ce stade, votre projet ne doit pas avoir commencé !
Liens liés à l'étape : [Déposer mon dossier](https://agirpourlatransition.ademe.fr/entreprises/aides-financieres/2024/realisation-dinstallations-production-chaleur-biomasse-bois?cible=79)
L'ADEME étudie votre demande en fonction de l’étude du projet, de l’approvisionnement biomasse, de la quantité de chaleur produite et de ses performances énergétiques et environnementales.
Si votre demande est acceptée, recevez un contrat de financement précisant le montant d’aide maximum, les conditions et les modalités de versement.
Réalisez vos investissements.

description:

- **définir un schéma directeur des réseaux**,

- **vérifier la faisabilité technique et économique du projet**,

- répondre aux conditions nécessaires pour bénéficier d’une aide à l’investissement.

description:
Vous cherchez à mieux gérer vos **biodéchets** et à en faire une ressource ? La CCI Hauts-de-France vous accompagne pour identifier les solutions de réduction et de valorisation adaptées à votre activité. Cet accompagnement vous aide à structurer une démarche concrète et efficace.

- Analysez la **nature, le volume et la fréquence** de vos biodéchets, ainsi que leur localisation.

- Repérez les solutions de **valorisation proches de chez vous** : compostage, méthanisation, etc.

- Référencez vos flux sur une **plateforme géolocalisée** dédiée pour faciliter les synergies locales.

- Bénéficiez d’un **outil d’aide à la décision** pour choisir les solutions techniques, repérer les dispositifs de financement mobilisables, et entrer en contact avec les bons interlocuteurs.

Projets liés au dispositif d'aide :
Gestion des biodéchets
Zéro perte en production

Montant de l'aide ou cout: De 750 à 3 500 € HT

Durée de l'aide: De 1 à 5 jours selon la taille et le secteur d'activité de l'entreprise

Contact public pour les questions sur le dispositif: https://mission-transition-ecologique.beta.gouv.fr/aides-entreprise/gestion-des-biodechets?utm_campaign=openData

Etapes pour activer le dispositif :
Contactez un conseiller via le formulaire dédié pour exprimer votre intérêt.
Liens liés à l'étape : [mission transition écologique](https://mission-transition-ecologique.beta.gouv.fr/aides-entreprise/gestion-des-biodechets?utm_campaign=openData)
Un conseiller vous rappelle pour répondre à vos questions et vous guider dans la constitution de votre demande.
Définissez avec l’expert le périmètre du diagnostic, la méthode et le calendrier.
Lancez le diagnostic avec l'expert proposé par votre CCI.

The credit guarantee is issued to companies that have insufficient collateral to obtain a loan or to obtain a loan of the required amount, but have a transparent financial history and a positive creditworthiness. Up to 80% of the principal amount of financing; up to EUR 25 million; up to 10 years. For guarantees submitted until 30.06.2026 the premium rate is 0% per year; for guarantees of EUR 5,000,000 the premium rate is applied according to the price list. ALTUM guarantee is not a guarantee within the meaning of the Civil Code of the Republic of Latvia, but state support in the form of a financial instrument (guarantee) for the receipt of a financial service in case of insufficient collateral; the obligation of ALTUM to be liable to the Financier for the unpaid principal amount does not exempt the Merchant (including the Guarantors) from the obligation to repay the full amount of the Financial Service Agreement.

eligibility_text: The beneficiary authorizes an accountable project leader who is in an employment relationship with the beneficiary or holds a position of responsibility in the company. A person disqualified from the practice of commercial activities cannot act as the accountable project leader. the beneficiary has confirmed the decision and these conditions Business Finland can finance SMEs and midcap companies seeking significant growth in export markets by granting grants or loans for ambitious R&D projects that provide the company with an international competitive advantage. A large company refers to a company that is not considered an SME under Article 2 of Annex I of the Block Exemption Regulation. At least 20% of the entire share capital or equivalent equity of another company is directly or indirectly owned or controlled by the other company a small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) is defined as a Finnish company with fewer than 250 employees A maximum of 50 per cent of the salaries allocated to the project are accepted as indirect personnel costs. A minimum of 10 per cent of the funding granted for the project will only be paid after the approval of the final report. A percentage of the salaries paid for effective working hours and approved for the project that is laid out in the project cost estimate (max. 50%) can be accepted as indirect personnel costs. In addition, SMEs can include the costs of initial applications for intellectual property rights incurred during the project in the purchased service costs. The level of funding may be up to 50%. Costs related to the IPR applications of large enterprises (incl. midcap companies), as defined by the EU, will not be approved. The final instalment of the loan is at least 20 per cent of the principal of the granted loan. The combined total funding that the project receives from the Funding Agency and other providers of public funding may not exceed the project’s maximum limit for public funding. We grant 50% grants for research projects in SMEs. When the content of the project is entirely industrial research*, we grant a grant of 60% of the total eligible costs of the project. For midcap companies, the grant is 40% for research projects. When the project content is entirely industrial research*, we grant a grant of 50% of the total eligible costs of the project. The prerequisite for Business Finland's financing is that the company has a credible overall financing plan for the duration of the project. 6.1 Grants A minimum of 10 per cent of the funding granted for the project will only be paid after the approval of the final report. The right to the granted funding expires if the beneficiary of the funding has not delivered the documents requested by the State Treasury or signed the promissory note within six months from the date of the loan advance payment decision. the Funding Agency may for extremely weighty reasons extend the loan period to a maximum of twenty years. The grace period may not exceed ten (10) years. As a rule, it can cover a maximum of 50% of the total cost of your project. For a justified reason, the loan can cover 70% of the total project costs. Your company can receive 30% of the loan financing granted for the project as an advance at the beginning of the project, and we will pay the rest based on the actual costs. Piloting can also be carried out in a customer's facilities, provided that it cannot be regarded as a commercial delivery and the customer does not provide funding for the project directly or indirectly. In other words, your company must always carry the risk of the piloting project's success. The portion of these measures cannot exceed 20% of the approved cost estimate. R&D funding can only be allocated to the costs arising from research and development activities. To ensure the effectiveness of the funding, only procurements and work ordered or agreed upon in writing after submitting the funding application are approved for the project.

eligibility_text: This guide outlines our standard approach to term sheets when CDP Venture Capital acts as the lead investor in an investment round. In the very early stages, we primarily use quasi-equity instruments such as SAFEs (Simple Agreements for Future Equity) or PFIs (Participating Financial Instruments). Equity investments occur through a capital increase, meaning the issuance of new shares or quotas subscribed by the investor. there is a product, a market, initial execution track record, and often a first set of metrics. CDP Venture Capital employs different investment instruments depending on the maturity of the startup and the market context. The anti-dilution clause, instead, allows the investor’s position to be recalibrated if the company raises capital at a lower valuation than the one at which the investor originally invested (a so-called down round). In the very early stages, the presence of a non-voting observer may be sufficient to grant the investor a channel that ensures ongoing visibility into the company’s activities. Beyond the Board of Directors, governance also includes reserved matters, that is, decisions requiring the active involvement of investors. they typically include a valuation cap, which sets the maximum valuation at which the instrument may convert into shares. other provisions may be included, such as a conversion floor, which sets a minimum conversion valuation and limits the dilutive impact on founders Another commonly used clause is the Most Favored Nation (MFN), which ensures that, at conversion, the investor receives the most favorable terms granted to any subsequent investor. It ensures that, primarily in the event of a sale or liquidation of the company, the investor has the right to recover at least the capital invested before proceeds are distributed to other shareholders. the Right of First Offer (ROFO), the right to purchase shares being sold by other shareholders before they are offered to third parties, helps maintain a coherent ownership structure over time Tag-along and drag-along rights are designed to transparently and orderly manage scenarios in which one or more shareholders decide to sell their stake. Additional mechanisms, such as sell mandates, are often introduced to explore IPO or M&A opportunities once the company reaches a certain stage of development.

description: Part-funded collaborative defence development that turns an existing design into hardware - prototyping, testing, qualification and certification of a defence product - where the EU pays only a slice of the cost and the consortium and its Member States carry the rest.
eligibility_text:
WHAT MAKES A DEVELOPMENT ACTION DIFFERENT FROM ITS ONLY SIBLING, THE RESEARCH ACTION:

1. YOU DO NOT GET 100%. Development actions are the only EDF leaf where the EU pays a fraction of eligible costs, and the fraction depends on which activity you are doing. Table 1 baseline rates: integrating knowledge up to 65%, studies up to 90%, design up to 65%, "The system prototyping of a defence Up to 20%", testing up to 45%, "The qualification of a defence product, Up to 70%", certification up to 70%, increasing efficiency up to 65%. Table 3 maxima after bonuses: prototyping up to 55%, testing/qualification/certification up to 80%, integrating knowledge / studies / design / increasing efficiency up to 100%. So the closer you get to a fieldable product, the less the EU pays - prototyping at a 20% baseline is the single sharpest number in the regime.

2. THE BONUS MACHINERY EXISTS ONLY HERE: "Table 2. Increase of funding rates (bonus) for development actions" - PESCO bonus +10%, SME bonus (proportion of eligible costs to EU SMEs, up to 5% for non-cross-border SMEs plus twice the proportion for cross-border SMEs), mid-cap bonus +10%. The overall increase cannot exceed 35% of the total eligible costs of the activity, and the result cannot exceed the Table 3 maxima. Derogation: "the activities carried out under the specific actions that target disruptive technologies under the EDF-2026-LS-DIS call and aim to develop technologies or assets that increase efficiency across the life cycle of defence products and technologies (Article 10.3(i) of the EDF Regulation) will be funded at 100%."

3. ACTIVITY TYPES ARE THE MATURITY GATE. System prototyping, testing, qualification, certification and increasing efficiency are eligible ONLY for development actions. Generating knowledge is NOT eligible for a development action at all - a DA proposal cannot be framed as new knowledge creation.

4. THE NO-PROFIT DEROGATION IS DA-SPECIFIC: "No profit rule: To ensure the continuity of the development actions after the period of EU financing provided for in the grant, potential revenue to be generated by these actions will not be taken into consideration in accordance with point (a) of Article 195(3) of the Financial Regulation."

5. TOPIC/CALL-LEVEL DA CONDITIONS (not all development actions):
- EDF-2026-DA-EXP (expedited): "Proposals should be submitted within a shorter timeframe than for EDF-2026-DA, and the evaluation process should be faster." EDF-2026-DA-ACC (accelerated): same submission timeframe, faster evaluation.
- EDF-2026-LS-DA-DIS: consortium of at least two legal entities in at least two different Member States or EDF associated countries, at least two of which are not controlled by the same legal entity and do not control each other - a lower floor than the standard Article 10(4) rule.

IMPORTANT NEGATIVE FINDING: the prior Member State commitment to procure / joint procurement, which is the textbook DA discriminator, is NOT written into the 2026 (or 2025 Part 2) work programme. The work programme delegates eligibility to "Articles 9 and 10(4) of the EDF Regulation" and uses that same phrase for the RA calls. Do not seed a procurement-commitment gate from this source.
name: Edf DA

description: Fully EU-funded collaborative defence R&D that stops before anything is built: knowledge generation, feasibility studies and design for defence products and technologies, delivered by a cross-border consortium of EU/associated-country entities.
eligibility_text:
WHAT MAKES A RESEARCH ACTION DIFFERENT FROM ITS ONLY SIBLING, THE DEVELOPMENT ACTION:

1. FUNDING RATE: research actions are funded at 100% of eligible costs for every activity type open to them, with no bonus machinery and no cap below 100%. In Table 1 (baseline) and Table 3 (maximum) the research-action column is 100% throughout, while the development-action column is capped: e.g. "Studies such as feasibility studies to explore 100% Up to 90%" and design "100% Up to 65%". The bonus table is explicitly headed "Table 2. Increase of funding rates (bonus) for development actions" - PESCO, SME and mid-cap bonuses are not available to a research action because it is already at 100%.

2. ACTIVITY TYPES. "The table below indicates which activities are eligible for research actions and which for development actions." Generating knowledge (activity (a)) is eligible for research actions and NOT eligible for development actions - it is the only RA-exclusive activity. Conversely system prototyping, testing, qualification, certification and increasing efficiency are not eligible under a research action at all, so an RA proposal may cover only generating knowledge, integrating knowledge, studies and design.

3. THE NO-PROFIT DEROGATION DOES NOT APPLY. The work programme's no-profit rule is written to "ensure the continuity of the development actions" only; RA revenue treatment is unchanged.

4. TOPIC-LEVEL RA CONDITIONS (do not apply to all research actions - flagged honestly):
- EDF-2026-LS-RA-SI (2 topics): "The proposals must build upon or integrate results that have been achieved within one or several projects that were funded under an EU programme call with a focus on civil applications." Applicants must confirm they have or will have the rights to use and commercialise those prior results. This is a spin-in-from-civil gate with no development-action equivalent.
- EDF-2026-LS-DIS-RA-SMERO-NT (1 topic): "Members of the consortium need to be SMEs (as defined in Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC) or research organisations. The coordinator of the consortium needs to be an SME. The budget allocated to research organisations cannot exceed 40% of the total requested grant amount."

PUT IN NEITHER LEAF because the 2026 work programme applies them identically to RA and DA: the consortium rule ("Any eligible consortium as defined in Articles 9 and 10(4) of the EDF Regulation" is the wording used for the RA calls AND the DA calls), non-EU ownership/effective-control conditions, the Member-State rights-to-use clause, the 25% flat indirect-cost rate, and TRL floors (topic-level on both sides: TRL 4 for both the RA and the DA non-thematic SME topics).
name: Edf RA

description: A EUR 150 000, 18-month lump sum that lets a current or recent ERC frontier-research grant holder test whether one specific result from that grant can become a product, a spin-out or a licence - you cannot apply unless you already hold, or recently held, the ERC grant it derives from.
eligibility_text:
ERC Proof of Concept is gated on an ERC grant the applicant already holds, which no other instrument in this programme requires. "The ERC Proof of Concept Grant is open to Principal Investigators whose ERC main frontier research grant is ongoing, or Principal Investigators whose ERC main frontier research grant ends on or after 1 January 2025, subject to restrictions provided in Annex 3 below." There is no route in for a company or a researcher without an ERC main grant.

The idea must also derive from that grant. "These grants are available only to Principal Investigators, whose proposals draw substantially on their ERC-funded research; therefore, applicants need to demonstrate the relation between the idea to be taken to proof of concept and their main grant." The same test is the award criterion: "The activities of the Proof of Concept Grant shall draw substantially on the research carried out as part of the main ERC frontier research grant."

The award and its duration are fixed rather than proposed. It is awarded as a single lump sum contribution of EUR 150 000 "for a period of eighteen months". Extensions may be granted when duly justified. The lump sum covers direct and indirect eligible costs and is paid regardless of costs actually incurred. Indicative call budget EUR 60 000 000.

A quota applies per parent grant. "A maximum of three Proof of Concept Grants may be awarded for a Starting, Consolidator, or Advanced Grant project, and a maximum of six Proof of Concept Grants - for a Synergy Grant project." Grants may run in parallel. A Synergy Principal Investigator may apply "only with the written consent of all Principal Investigators of the same Synergy Grant project", and each may submit one application. A Principal Investigator may submit only one proposal to this call under this Work Programme; two cut-off rounds run in the year and only the first admissible and eligible proposal is evaluated.

The applicant is a single Principal Investigator, not a consortium. "Proposals for the Proof of Concept Grant call are submitted by the Principal Investigator on behalf of the Host Institution", and a binding Host Institution Support Letter must be supplied at the time of application or the proposal may be declared inadmissible. Consortium agreements are not required, and "Excellence is the sole criterion of evaluation." A Principal Investigator rejected for a breach of research integrity under Work Programme 2024 or Work Programme 2025 may not apply.

description: Grants of roughly EUR 1.2m to EUR 20m per project to take bio-based feedstock - agricultural and forestry residues, bio-waste, side streams - through biorefining into chemicals, materials, fibres, packaging, food ingredients or crop inputs, from lab proof (TRL 3-5) all the way to a first full industrial-scale biorefinery (TRL 8), with the industry consortium expected to put in its own money as in-kind contribution.
eligibility_text:
These are Joint Undertaking conditions, and they do not appear in a Commission-run Horizon cluster.

In-kind contribution is scored, not merely recorded. Under Impact, proposals are assessed on their ability to reach the level of in-kind contribution to operational activities set for the topic, expressed as a percentage of total eligible project costs: 5% for research and innovation actions, 15% for innovation actions and 20% for Flagship innovation actions. IKOP means "Contributions by private members, constituent entities or the affiliated entities of either, by international organisations and by contributing partners, consisting of the eligible costs incurred by them in implementing indirect actions less the contribution of that joint undertaking and of the participating states of that joint undertaking to those costs." A consortium carrying no private-member industry cannot generate IKOP and scores badly on Impact.

Private membership must be evidenced in the proposal itself: "Innovation Actions, including Flagships, and Research and Innovation Actions: For all legal entities that are members of the BIC consortium, a certification from BIC attesting to this fact should be included in the proposal". BIC is the Bio-based Industries Consortium, the private member of the Joint Undertaking.

Flagship topics are a separate track with heavier requirements. They require, in a dedicated annex, "a detailed business plan, which should include an estimate of appropriate economic indicators, including Net Present Value (NPV), with all critical underlying assumptions clearly defined and appropriately justified", and "Only for Flagship topics: As part of the panel review, the CBE JU will organise hearings with applicants of all Flagships proposals." Research and innovation actions need only a qualitative business case, and non-Flagship innovation actions a quantified business case and business model.

Feedstock is constrained by origin and by principle. Every research and innovation action, innovation action and Flagship must describe bio-based feedstock within the scope of the Joint Undertaking's strategic research agenda and "use bio-based feedstock that is both produced (or generated) and processed in EU Member States and/or countries associated to Horizon Europe", with evidence on climate, biodiversity, pollution and water. Subject to the food-first and cascading-use principles, "agricultural biomass can be used as feedstock for CBE JU projects". Innovation actions and Flagships must forecast agricultural-biomass volumes and assess interference with the food supply chain.

Life-cycle sustainability assessment is mandatory: an ex-ante environmental assessment for every action type, plus an ex-post dedicated task for research and innovation actions or a work package for innovation actions and Flagships. A multi-actor approach is required for all types of action.

Maturity is set high for deployment. "IAs projects are demonstration activities in relevant and operational environments and expected to deliver TRL 6-8 at the end of the projects. In particular, Flagship projects will need to deliver TRL 8 at the end of the projects." Research and innovation actions deliver TRL 3-5.

Every 2026 grant topic carries an intellectual-property derogation: "The granting authority may, up to 4 years after the end of the action, object to a transfer of ownership or to the exclusive licensing of results", as set out in the specific provision of Annex 5.

description: Collaborative R&I grants for health research that generates clinical evidence — disease prevention and treatment, vaccines and medical countermeasures, health-system transformation, and the tools and cohorts behind them — for consortia that usually run or plan clinical studies.
eligibility_text: Cluster 1 Health's discriminating condition runs the opposite way from the security clusters: it widens the eligible-country set rather than narrowing it. On 37 distinct pages the Eligibility conditions row states "In recognition of the opening of the US National Institutes of Health’s programmes to European researchers, any legal entity established in the United States of America is eligible to receive Union funding." On Coordination and Support Action topics the same reciprocity is granted in a narrower form — US entities "may exceptionally participate as a beneficiary or affiliated entity, and are eligible to receive Union funding" — paired with a derogation from the standard consortium rule in the other direction: "Coordinators of projects must be legal entities established in an EU Member State or Associated Country." No other Pillar II cluster opens funding eligibility to US entities as a standing rule. Second, the cluster is organised around clinical evidence generation and defines its own unusually broad object: "In the context of the Health Cluster Work Programme part for 2026-2027, a clinical study covers clinical studies/trials/investigations/cohorts and is defined as any systematic prospective or retrospective collection and analysis of health data obtained from individual patients or healthy persons" — explicitly wider than Regulation 536/2014, and topics repeatedly note that "As proposals under this topic are expected to include clinical studies, the use of the template is strongly encouraged", the template being a dedicated clinical-studies annex in the submission system. Third, many topics carry a binding SSH requirement: "This topic requires the effective contribution of social sciences and humanities (SSH) disciplines and the involvement of SSH experts". Fourth, the co-funded European Partnership topics derogate from the standard funding rates: "The funding rate is 50% of the eligible costs." (Rare Diseases) and "The funding rate is 30% of the eligible costs." (Personalised Medicine). Notably, unlike Clusters 3 and 4, this part states no TRL in any topic conditions table (zero TRL rows across 211 pages), and Article 22(5) participation limits appear on only one topic (page 173), so an applicant's country eligibility here is broader than in the security or space clusters, not tighter.

description: Collaborative R&I and innovation grants for civil security technology — fighting crime and terrorism, border and customs control, disaster resilience, infrastructure protection and cybersecurity — where the consortium must include the public authorities who would actually operate the result.
eligibility_text: The discriminating condition in Cluster 3 is a mandatory end-user beneficiary quota written into almost every topic's Eligibility conditions row under "The following additional eligibility conditions apply:". Typical wording: "This topic requires the active involvement, as beneficiaries, of at least 3 Police Authorities 47 from at least 3 different EU Member States or Associated Countries." The definition is deliberately narrow: ‘Police Authorities’ means "public authorities explicitly designated by national law, or other entities legally mandated by the competent national authority, for the prevention, detection and/or investigation of terrorist offences or other criminal offences, specifically excluding police academies, forensic institutes, training facilities as well as border and customs authorities". The required practitioner class tracks the destination: Police Authorities (2 or 3, on many topics alongside at least 2 Civil Society Organisations or NGOs) for Fighting Crime and Terrorism; "at least 2 Border or Coast Guard Authorities from at least 2 different EU Member States or Associated Countries" for Border Management; "at least 2 Customs Authorities from at least 2 different EU Member States or Associated Countries"; first responders, medical emergency authorities or authorities in charge of disaster risk for Disaster-Resilient Society; and on PCP/PPI topics "practitioners and 3 public procurers. These beneficiaries must be from at least 3 different EU Member States or Associated Countries." Named practitioners must be declared in the "Information about security practitioners" table in the application form. Second, every topic states a TRL band in its conditions table (40 such rows in this part, ranging TRL 4 to TRL 8), e.g. "Activities are expected to achieve TRL 6-8 by the end of the project"; the Health work programme states none. Third, on innovation actions in critical technology areas the cluster activates the General Annex control test: "entities established in an eligible country but which are directly or indirectly controlled by China or by a legal entity established in China are not eligible to participate in the action" (16 topic tables). Fourth, topic tables carry a Security Sensitive Topics row on classified background and EUCI/SEN results — "Please refer to the related provisions in section B Security — EU classified and sensitive information of the General Annexes." Fifth, the 2026 cybersecurity budget is run by a delegated body: "The Commission intends to conclude a contribution agreement with the European Cybersecurity Competence Centre (ECCC)", whose call is limited under Article 22(5) so that participation "is limited to legal entities established in Member States and Associated Countries" with entities controlled by a non-eligible country excluded outright.

description: Collaborative R&I and innovation grants for the EU's technology sovereignty stack — AI, quantum, photonics, semiconductors, advanced materials and manufacturing, circular industry, raw materials and space — where eligibility is gated on where the applicant is established and who ultimately controls it.
eligibility_text: Cluster 4's discriminating condition is a per-topic patchwork of bespoke eligible-country lists invoked under Article 22(5), replacing the standard Member State or Associated Country test with something narrower or wider depending on the technology. Space topics are the tightest: "In order to achieve the expected outcomes, and safeguard the Union’s strategic assets, interests, autonomy, or security, participation is limited to legal entities established in Member States, Norway and Iceland." One EU Space Surveillance and Tracking topic goes further: "participation is limited to legal entities established in Member States. Proposals including entities established in countries outside the scope specified in the call/topic/action will be ineligible." Digital and semiconductor topics use an intermediate list — "participation is limited to legal entities established in Member States, Iceland and Norway and the following additional associated countries: Canada, Israel, Republic of Korea, New Zealand, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom." Raw-materials topics widen it instead: "participation in this topic is limited to legal entities established in Member States, associated countries, OECD countries, African Union Member States, MERCOSUR, CARIFORUM, Andean Community and countries with which the EU has concluded strategic partnerships on raw materials". On restricted topics an ownership test also applies: "entities established in an eligible country listed above, but which are directly or indirectly controlled by a non-eligible country or by a non-eligible country entity, may not participate in the action unless it can be demonstrated, by means of guarantees positively assessed by their eligible country of establishment". Second, space topics use a different TRL yardstick entirely: "The reference TRL definition is the ISO 16290:2013 applicable to the space sector." Third, the cluster derogates from the standard consortium rule in both directions: Fast Track to Research and Innovation topics impose a ceiling — "The following additional eligibility criteria apply: consortia may include a maximum of 6 independent eligible entities as participants." — while a quantum inertial-navigation topic drops the three-entity floor entirely: "The following additional eligibility criteria apply: Proposals must be submitted by a single legal entity (mono-beneficiary CSA) wich is an SME." Fourth, one space topic derogates from the standard IA rate: "This is an Innovation Action (IA) with reduced funding rate (45%)." A space-security topic also imports the Cluster 3 practitioner mechanic, requiring "participation, as beneficiaries, of at least two crisis or security practitioner 190 organisations or agencies, established in at least two different EU Member States or Associated Countries."
name: Horizon EU CL4

description: Collaborative R&D and demonstration grants for decarbonising energy and transport — batteries and energy storage, renewables and grids, renewable fuels, CO2 capture and storage, road/rail/air/waterborne mobility, and the climate science underneath — with each topic naming the technology-readiness band the project must reach by its end.
eligibility_text: Cluster 5's leaf-level conditions are written per topic in a Technology Readiness Level row and in geographic derogations that no other cluster carries in this combination. 69 topics state an explicit band — "Activities are expected to achieve TRL 4-5 by the end of the project" through "Activities are expected to achieve TRL 7-8 by the end of the project", each closed by "see General Annex B. Activities may start at any TRL." — and 52 of those 69 require TRL 6 or above, so most CL5 money buys demonstration and first-of-a-kind scale-up, not lab work. Second, and unusually heavy for Pillar II, 61 distinct pages attach an exploitation lock to the grant: "The granting authority may, up to 4 years after the end of the action, object to a transfer of ownership or to the exclusive licensing of results, as set out in the specific provision of Annex 5." (Cluster 6 carries this on 6 pages, Missions on 13.) Third, several topics widen or bend the consortium rule on a sectoral-diplomacy basis. Africa-facing climate topics state "Due to the scope of this topic, legal entities established in all African Union member states are exceptionally eligible for Union funding." together with "At least 30% of the beneficiaries must be legal entities established in the African Union member states". Global-climate topics require that "the consortium must include as beneficiary or associated partner at least three independent legal entities established in three different low or lower/upper-middle-income countries". An EU-India battery topic runs the other way: "The project must include at least one work package for coordinated activities with the linked project awarded by the Ministry of Heavy Industry of the Government of India (MHI). Participation of legal entities established in India, which is a third country under Horizon Europe, is only possible as associated partners." Fourth, demonstration topics can force public bodies into the consortium: on the rural shared-mobility topic, "Each proposal must include pilot demonstrations in at least 4 pilot sites" and "The pilots must be community-driven, carried out under the lead or with the involvement of rural/local/regional public authorities/administrations and the local transport authorities, and these entities must be included in the consortium as beneficiaries." Finally, on ~10 grid, AI-for-energy and connected-vehicle Innovation Action topics: "entities established in an eligible country but which are directly or indirectly controlled by China or by a legal entity established in China are not eligible to participate in the action." Note these are topic-level rules, not a single cluster-wide gate: an applicant must read the topic's own conditions table.
name: Horizon EU CL5

description: Collaborative research and innovation grants for food systems, farming, forestry, fisheries and aquaculture, biodiversity, soil, water, the circular bioeconomy and rural/coastal/urban communities — where on most topics farmers, foresters, fishers, advisors and other end-users must sit inside the consortium as co-creators, not as an advisory board.
eligibility_text: Cluster 6's discriminating condition is the multi-actor approach, and it is an eligibility condition, not an ambition. 40 of the 69 topic conditions tables carry "The proposals must apply the multi-actor approach. See definition of the multi-actor approach in this work programme part." The definition, set out in a dedicated section 'Specific conditions for multi-actor projects', binds the consortium's composition and method: "A multi-actor project ensures the genuine and sufficient involvement of a targeted array of actors in co-creation, which serves the objectives of the project proposal." Topic texts translate this into named practitioner classes: "Proposals must implement the multi-actor approach, with a consortium based on a balanced mix of relevant actors with complementary knowledge clearly activating advisors, farmers and/or foresters and/or rural actors." It also imposes a deliverable no sibling cluster requires: "the new knowledge and innovation generated by the multi-actor projects must be summarised in an appropriate number of ‘practice abstracts’ in the common EIP-AGRI format for Horizon". Second, a set of place-based topics require named territorial demonstrators inside the consortium as beneficiaries. Living-lab topics: "at least five (5) distinct ‘living labs’ linked to regional or local authorities (and possibly together with their public and/or private ecosystem actors operating in their respective territories) must be part of the consortium as beneficiaries, among which at least two (2) living labs must be from different demonstration sites and another three (3) from other and different replication sites. 1 out of the 3 replication sites must be located in Horizon Europe widening countries (including Outermost Regions)." A rural/urban replication topic goes further: "at least nine (9) distinct regional or local authorities must be part of the consortium as beneficiaries, among which at least three (3) from different demonstration cities/regions and another six (6) from other and different replication cities/regions." Third, geographic derogations are common: "due to the specific challenge of this topic, in addition to the minimum number of participants set out in the General Annexes, consortia must include at least three independent legal entities established in an African Union member state"; "Due to the scope of this topic, legal entities established in Brazil are exceptionally eligible for Union funding."; "All international organisations are exceptionally eligible for funding."; and on one topic "the participation of at least one research institution or relevant public authority from Ukraine in the consortium is mandatory." Fourth, two partnership-continuation topics collapse the consortium rule to a single named applicant, e.g. "The proposal must be submitted by the coordinator of the consortium funded under HORIZON-CL6-2022-GOVERNANCE-01-02 and HORIZON-CL6-2024-GOVERNANCE-01-1: European Partnership for a climate neutral, sustainable and productive Blue Economy." These are effectively closed to new entrants.
name: Horizon EU CL6

description: Grants that build the plumbing of Europe's startup economy rather than funding startups directly — networks of deep-tech startup and scaleup hubs, technology transfer offices, cross-border acceleration, innovation procurement and philanthropy links — with the money typically passed on to companies as cascade sub-grants of EUR 60,000 to EUR 200,000.
eligibility_text: European Innovation Ecosystems is the only Pillar II leaf whose eligibility rules are about who represents an ecosystem, and every one of its five 2026-2027 topics derogates from the standard consortium rule. The flagship COFUND topic (European Startup and Scaleup Hubs pilot, EUR 20m to one project) requires: "A hub must be represented by a single legal entity (for instance an umbrella organisation representing a science and technology park or an innovation cluster or district, an accelerator or a venture builder embedded in an innovation ecosystem) or several legal entities representing the relevant actors of the innovation ecosystem supporting startups"; "The consortium should consist of a network of at least ten (10) hubs from at least ten (10) different Member States or Associated Countries."; a population-based cap — "For Member States and Associated Countries with an overall population exceeding 35 million, the participation is limited to two hubs in the given consortium. In addition, at least two (2) participating hub shall be established in a “widening country”." (one hub only for countries under 35 million); and a co-financing proof at submission: "The consortium must provide a single letter of intent at the moment of submission of the proposal indicating the source of the required 50% of complementary funding (e.g. national and/or regional funding, EU funding, or private investments)." Other topics restrict who may be a beneficiary or coordinator by organisation type: the TTO topic requires "This action requires the participation, as beneficiaries, of at least three (3) legal entities from at least three (3) different Member States or" "Associated Countries that are universities, research and higher education institutions or research technology organisations (RTOs)." plus "In addition, at least one (1) legal entity shall be established in a “widening country”." The philanthropy topic states "The coordinator of the project must be a higher education institution, or research technology organisation(s) (RTOs) or a network of such organisations." and "Consortia must include at least three (3) participants from three (3) different member states or associated countries, including higher education institution(s) or RTOs and philanthropy organisation(s) or network of philanthropy organisations." Startup Europe imposes an innovation-performance quota: at least 50% of beneficiaries must be established in "'moderate' or ‘emerging’ innovator countries or regions. The Regional Innovation Scoreboard is taken as a reference, and in the case of entities representing national authorities, the European Innovation Scoreboard." Cascade funding is central rather than incidental: "Beneficiaries may provide financial support to third parties. The support to third parties can only be provided in the form of grants. The maximum amount to be granted to each third party is EUR 60 000." on the hubs and Startup Europe topics, and "The maximum amount to be granted to each third party is EUR 200 000 to ensure the deployment and impact of the project outcomes." on the PCP topic. No topic in this part states a TRL.
name: Horizon EU EIE

description: Grants that implement five named EU Missions — Adaptation to Climate Change, Cancer, 100 Climate-Neutral and Smart Cities, Restore our Ocean and Waters, and A Soil Deal for Europe — funding demonstration and replication in real territories, where the cities, regions or living labs are beneficiaries of the grant rather than study subjects.
eligibility_text: The Missions work programme covers all five EU Missions — "Adaptation to Climate Change", "Cancer", "100 Climate-Neutral and Smart cities by 2030", "Restore our Ocean and Waters by 2030" and "A Soil Deal for Europe" — plus joint calls between them. Its discriminating conditions are membership conditions: the beneficiary must be, or must come from, a place that has already joined the Mission. The Cities Mission and its joint calls repeatedly require: "At least three cities, represented by a local authority or by an entity with an explicit consent from the local authority, each from a different Member State or Associated Country, must participate as beneficiaries." and "At least one of the three cities must be one of the 112 cities selected for the EU Mission on Climate-Neutral and Smart Cities". A two-city variant exists, and a lead/follower variant: "At least three lead cities, represented by a local authority or by an entity with an explicit consent from the local authority, from different Member States or Associated Countries along with at least three follower cities, must participate ensuring a good geographical balance." Joint Cities/Adaptation topics add a charter test: "Entities from at least four cities, each from a different Member State or Associated Country, must participate as beneficiaries." and "at least one must be a signatory to the Adaptation Mission Charter" — the Charter being the instrument by which, per this document, "more than 325 regional and local authorities have committed to working together to transition faster to a climate resilient Europe." Demonstration geography is also prescribed: "Demonstration activities must take place in the territory of at least 3 different regional or local authorities that host cultural heritage, each established in a different Member State or Associated Country." and, on a cross-border topic, "The demonstration areas must span adjacent regions on both sides of a national border." The Soil Mission carries CL6-style conditions: "Proposals must apply the multi-actor approach. See definition of the multi-actor approach in the introduction to this work programme part." on 9 topic pages, plus a biogeographic constraint — "regions: Alpine or Atlantic, i.e., the majority of the living labs of each proposal must be located in one of these two biogeographical regions." — and living-lab cascade funding: "Beneficiaries may provide financial support to third parties to facilitate active involvement of smaller actors (e.g. land managers and owners such as farmers, SMEs or civil societies) in one or more of the living labs of the project." One Adaptation topic makes cascade funding compulsory and unusually large: "Beneficiaries must provide financial support to third parties. The support to third parties can only be provided in the form of grants. The maximum amount to be granted to each third party is EUR 800,000" — the only 'must' FSTP clause in the part, against 14 'may' clauses.

description: The UK's national innovation agency, part of UK Research and Innovation. Awards grant funding to UK-registered businesses for innovation projects through a rolling programme of individual competitions, applied for through the Innovation Funding Service.
eligibility_text: Innovate UK largely requires that projects are led by businesses; other types of organisations can apply in collaboration with a business partner. To be eligible as a UK-registered business you must have a Companies House registration number; a registration number that does not relate to a fully registered UK business will not be eligible to apply for funding, for example FC or BR prefixes. Businesses registered in the Channel Islands, Isle of Man or Crown Dependencies are not eligible for funding as a UK business. Applicants must carry out their project activities in the UK. Research and technology organisations may lead only where the competition allows them to lead, or where no business in the consortium has the capacity to lead the project, and must partner with two or more businesses. Collaborative projects must have at least two grant-claiming partners and evidence of an effective collaboration, and one partner must not account for more than 70% of the eligible costs. The definition of micro, small and medium-sized enterprise used by Innovate UK is set out in the company accounts guidance, and when selecting your business category you must take into account any ownership, interest or association with a parent company or group of companies; a large business in this context means any enterprise which is not an SME. Research organisations undertaking non-economic activity are funded at 80% of full economic costs if an academic institution and 100% of eligible costs for all other research organisations; public sector organisations and charities conducting research with no economic benefit may receive 100% of their eligible costs. The grant funding rate a business receives depends on the size and type of the organisation and its role in the project. NOTE ON SCOPE: these are Innovate UK's standing funding rules, which apply across its portfolio. Innovate UK does not award against these rules directly -- it awards through individual time-limited COMPETITIONS, each of which publishes its own binding eligibility, scope and deadline on the Innovation Funding Service. The competition's own brief governs.
name: Innovate UK

Distinguishing feature within the Innovation Fund regime: it is not a grant call at all but a COMPETITIVE AUCTION - bidders compete on a requested subsidy in EUR per kilogram, and the award is a fixed premium paid only against verified certified RFNBO production over up to 10 years of operation. Payout is therefore contingent on delivered volume rather than fixed at signature, which is why award amounts recorded against this lot are ceilings.

eligibility_text: An Industrial PhD project is a collaboration between a company, a university and an Industrial PhD student. Have a branch with an independent CVR number and geographically located in Denmark2. The Industrial PhD student is employed and can perform his or her work for the company here. Be a university or a higher educational institution in Denmark or abroad that is officially approved to conduct a PhD programme. Have the finances and facilities to manage the project throughout the entire project period. Not be subject to compulsory dissolution, bankruptcy, voluntary liquidation or suspension of payments. Have complied with any repayment orders issued by the European Commission in one or more decisions where state aid granted by the Danish authorities has been found illegal and incompatible with the internal market. Must not be an ‘undertaking in difficulty’ as defined in Article 2 (1), No. 18 of the Commission Regulation (EU) No. 651/2014 of 17 June 2014 declaring certain categories of aid compatible with the internal market pursuant to Articles 107 and 108 of the Treaty. If the host university for the Industrial PhD programme is located outside Denmark, up to DKK 122,000 will be given as an additional grant for travel and accommodation at the university. Please note that a maximum of 50 % of a company's total expenses for an Industrial PhD project may be financed by public funds. Innovation Fund Denmark finances up to DKK 17,000 per month of the Industrial PhD student's salary for three years. However, a maximum 50% of the total salary (actual salary expenses calculated on the basis of the annual gross salary, including pension, insurance and holiday pay) can be covered. in as far as the part of the project receiving funding must in its entirety fall within “industrial research” as defined in the General Block Exemption Regulation article 2 (84) and (85). The company will also have DKK 100,000 available for the Industrial PhD student's • travels ... and • participation in PhD courses that yield ECTS points and are not offered at the host university. Innovation Fund Denmark gives the university a fixed amount of DKK 360,000 (incl. overhead) to cover: Have a project-relevant education completed with a master's degree. the company and the university must find a candidate who meets the requirements within six months from the date the grant is awarded. the Industrial PhD student must be employed full time in the company and thus work under the conditions that apply for private employment. The student's work assignments and time must be fully allocated to the Industrial PhD project and programme The Industrial PhD student's total salary (the sum of salary and pension) must at least correspond to the total salary for PhD fellows employed in the state as determined in the relevant collective agreement. Innovation Fund Denmark reserves the right to discontinue the project if the PhD degree has not been achieved within five years after the start of the project (excluding leaves of absence). The duration of the project corresponds to the duration of the education programme, which in Denmark is three years. If the project exceeds three years, for example in the case of a foreign PhD programme, Innovation Fund Denmark will only finance the project for the final three years. The company and the university must immediately notify the Fund if there are significant changes in the premises for the grant. Non-compete clauses or the like in the employment contract must not limit the possibility for the student to obtain employment elsewhere. The Innovation Fund Denmark aims to process applications within 13 weeks. Irrespective of those limits, the public funding for the company may not exceed 50 % of the company’s eligible project costs. In a Danish PhD programme, the student must gain experience with knowledge dissemination related to the PhD project, cf. Chapter 3, Section 7 of the Danish PhD Regulation.

eligibility_text: Any legal entity (such as an enterprise, a research institution, or a public institution) in or outside Denmark and directly involved in the project activities is eligible to apply, participate, and receive funding from IFD. However, the main applicant in the application must be a Danish legal entity. An application must have at least two project participants of which at least one is not a public university. For the Grand Solutions call on quantum technologies, it is acceptable with at least two separate departments at the same public university as participants. An applicant who previously has received aid that has been declared incompatible with the internal market according to the European Commission, and who has not repaid such aid at the time of submitting the application to IFD, cannot receive an investment from IFD. An investment from IFD must not contravene national or international sanctions, including sanctions on the freezing of funds or prohibitions on direct and indirect provision. The duration of a Grand Solutions project must be between one and five years, and the IFD investment can contribute with a maximum of 75.0% of the total project budget1. The amount applied for must be between the lower and upper IFD investment limit constraints as specified in the call texts. Investments up to EUR 300,000 under the Grand Solutions programme may be granted pursuant to the conditions for de minimis aid set out in the de minimis regulation26. The total amount of de minimis aid granted to any enterprise, including from other entities than IFD, shall not exceed EUR If none of the above conditions are met, the IFD maximum investment rate for the project participant will be 15.0% lower than the rates in Tables 2 to 4. a maximum of 10.0% of IFD’s budgeted investment can be left undistributed among the individual participants in the full budget for phase 2 of a Grand Solutions call. IFD requires that all project participants invest in the project. The financial commitment from the individual project participants must reflect the value creation of the project for each participant and the project consortium. Please note that an IFD investment can only cover costs defrayed after the start of the investment period and before its expiry. The duration of the project must be between one and five years. no applicant can receive funding from IFD for activities supported by any other public sector subsidisation schemes within the EU or EU member states, including Denmark, unless this has been explicitly authorised in writing by IFD. If activities in a project in IFD’s assessment have received or will receive funding from a public body (local, regional or national authority; public fund; international publicly funded body; or similar), the project will in its entirety not be eligible for investment by IFD. In total, the total time from the submission deadline for letters of interest in phase 1 of the call and to a final response to the application in phase 2 of the call is expected to be 8-9 months. The evaluation time for phase 2 is expected to be approximately 12 weeks. All texts in the letter of interest form and appendix must be written in English. In the event of failure to comply with formal requirements or deadlines, the letter of interest will be rejected without substantive consideration. The budget overview must contain at least two project participants. The main applicant is under an obligation to notify IFD immediately in the event of any subsequent material changes that affect the information submitted in the letter of interest, including changes in the amount of funding for the activities or parts thereof received from other sources. The project described in your application for phase 2 must be the same project that was outlined in your letter of interest for phase 1, but adjustments within the limits described below are allowed.

eligibility_text: Only registered legal Danish entities are eligible for investments from IFD in an international project. Foreign partners can be subcontracted after approval by IFD. Registration on the e-grant portal is a pre-condition for possible future investment from IFD. State aid received by the grant recipient in the form of public grants, including EU co-finance, must be included in the assessment of aid intensity and the maximum amount limit. The global maximum for IFD investment to cooperation projects is 75% of the total project costs. If a Danish public partner or a large enterprise participating without having a Danish SME participating on an even basis, the investment rate is reduced by 50%. After applying for the international programme on the international portal, Danish participants in an international project must register on e-grant and upload their international application. Such funding/guarantees might be offset in the investment which IFD provides or has provided, thus the maximal co-financing percentage/the guarantee coverage offered by IFD and others is identical to the maximal co-financing IFD can provide without such alternative cofounding. The progress report must be submitted every six months unless otherwise agreed. The auditor's statement must be submitted annually. If the grant recipient has obtained or expects to obtain funding and/or guarantees from other public schemes, including EU schemes or municipal schemes for the same activities, IFD must be notified immediately. Danish project partners must fill in a final report on completion or termination of the project. All costs shall be reported after deduction of possible discounts, bonuses, etc. The financial report must be submitted to IFD no later than 60 days following the end of each period. Private enterprises, GTS-institutes, private organisations or public organisations not audited by the National Court of Auditors (Rigsrevisionen) must annually have all costs claimed in the financial reports controlled by an independent certified auditor. At the end of the project a Final Report must be submitted to IFD from each of the Danish participants no later than 60 days after completion of the project. A signed consortium agreement shall be sent to IFD and to the programme secretariats prior to the start of the project. When the project is mentioned in printed or electronic material, the programmes and IFD's logos must be used. A reference to the IFD investment and EU co-funding must be highlighted in the text.

I resten av utlysningen bruker vi fellesbetegnelsen "bedrift". Enkeltpersonforetak kan ikke være prosjektansvarlige, men de kan være samarbeidspartnere. Prosjektansvarlig og samarbeidspartnere må være uavhengige av hverandre. Med dette mener vi at den ene ikke kan ha kontrollerende innflytelse over den andre. Norske bedrifter som skal være samarbeidspartnere må oppfylle de samme kriteriene som prosjektansvarlig for å kunne delta i prosjektet og motta støtte. Vi anser søknader med gjennomsnittskarakter ≥3 og ingen delkarakter ≤2, som støtteverdige og vil behandle disse videre. Alle andre søknader blir avslått. Forskningsrådet kan avvise søknader der prosjektansvarlig eller samarbeidspartner de siste to årene før innsendt søknad vesentlig har misligholdt sine forpliktelser i andre prosjekter med støtte fra Forskningsrådet. Søknaden kan bli avvist dersom prosjektleder er felt i Felles redelighetsutvalg eller Granskningsutvalget de siste to årene før innsendt søknad. Støtte kan ikke gis til foretak som ikke har oppfylt krav om tilbakebetaling etter en forutgående beslutning fra ESA/EU-kommisjonsbeslutning der støtten er erklært ulovlig og uforenlig med det indre marked. Støtte kan heller ikke gis til foretak i vanskeligheter i EØS-rettslig forstand. Ordningen skal praktiseres i tråd med EØS-avtalens statsstøtteregler. Vilkår og begreper skal tolkes i tråd med korresponderende vilkår og begreper i støttereglene. Ved eventuell motstrid mellom utlysningen og statsstøttereglene, skal sistnevnte ha forrang. Dere kan ikke ha startet noen av aktivitetene i prosjektet før dere sender inn søknaden. Seneste tidspunkt for oppstart av prosjektet vil være fire måneder etter at dere får beskjed om tildelingen. Prosjekter som ikke har startet innen dette tidspunktet, kan miste tildelingen. Seneste tidspunkt for oppstart av prosjektet vil være fire måneder etter at dere får beskjed om tildelingen. Dere kan bare søke om støtte til prosjektet én gang hvert kalenderår uavhengig av hvilken IPN-utlysning det gjelder. Denne utlysningen har løpende søknadsmottak og -behandling fra utlysningen åpner. Støtte fra andre offentlige aktører til prosjektet eller til aktiviteter som inngår i prosjektet, vil kunne påvirke omfanget av Forskningsrådets støtte. Alle partnerne skal ha definerte oppgaver og en tydelig rolle i gjennomføringen av prosjektet. Det er en betingelse for å få støtte at samarbeidspartnerne og FoU-leverandørene kommer til å delta i prosjektet slik som beskrevet i søknaden. Dersom dere endrer prosjektsammensetningen før dere får tilskuddsbrev fra oss, kan vi trekke tilbake tilsagnet om finansiering. Samarbeidspartnere skal inngå i faktisk samarbeid med prosjektansvarlig, noe som blant annet innebærer at de deler både risikoen og resultatene som kommer ut av prosjektet. FoU-leverandører skal ikke bidra til å finansiere prosjektet, og har derfor vanligvis ikke rettigheter til prosjektresultatene. De leverer et arbeid på oppdrag, og får betalt for dette arbeidet til markedspris. Får dere statsstøtte fra oss som tilsvarer 100 000 euro eller mer, vil vi gjøre det kjent i Registeret for offentlig støtte (lenken åpnes i nytt vindu). Prosjektleder og prosjektansvarlig skal ha vurdert og håndtert hensynet til forskningssikkerhet i prosjektet. Forskningsrådet stiller krav om full og umiddelbar åpen tilgang (open access) for vitenskapelige artikler, se Plan S - åpen tilgang til publikasjoner .
